_source: OSRS Wiki, Grand Exchange page, 'Convenience fee and item sink'.
_verified: July 2026, cross-checked name by name against a live /mapping.
_note: The wiki API exposes no tax-exempt flag, so this list is maintained by hand. Names are matched case-insensitively against /mapping and any name that matches nothing is reported by the CLI and the dashboard — check that count after every game update rather than trusting this file.
_naming_traps: Teleports are listed on the wiki by spell name but appear in /mapping as '<place> teleport (tablet)'. Civitas illa fortis is the exception and carries no suffix.
Only the fully charged Games necklace(8) and Ring of dueling(8) are GE-tradeable; partially used jewellery cannot be traded at all, so lower charges are not items to exempt.
Watering can has no charge suffix in /mapping; the charged variants are untradeable.
Poisoned dart naming is inconsistent in the game data: 'Iron dart (p)' has a space, 'Bronze dart(p)' and 'Steel dart(p)' do not.
_assumption: Poisoned dart variants are assumed to inherit the base dart's exemption. Unverified — the wiki lists only the base darts.
